title: Frostbite: Yeeeow!
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss frostbite: why it happens, how it relates to hypothermia, the body's shutting off of blood flow to extremities (hunting response), ice crystal damage to cells, the four degrees of frostbite, and the freeze-thaw problem. They cover warm-water rewarming versus direct heat, reperfusion injury, infection risk, prevention through layered breathable clothing, and myths about body fat, alcohol and cigarettes. They tell the story of Olympic wrestler Rulon Gardner's frostbite after being stranded on a snowmobile, note racial-descent differences in frostbite rates among soldiers, and mention body parts at risk. The episode opens with election-day banter and a Sketch Fest promo, and closes with a listener mail item about burglar tape from Josh Hines.

segments.title: Sketch Fest promo and election day banter
segments.summary: Josh promotes a live Sketch Fest show in San Francisco and the hosts chat about Election Day, early voting, and thanking election volunteers before turning to frostbite.

segments.title: Rulon Gardner's frostbite story and who gets frostbite
segments.summary: The hosts recount Olympic Greco-Roman wrestler Rulon Gardner's 2000 Olympic gold and his later snowmobile stranding in extreme cold that left him with frostbite and a lost toe. They note frostbite was historically a military injury and has become more common with winter sports, and mention higher rates among some ethnic groups and men aged 30 to 49.

segments.title: Personal cold experiences and the Browns game
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck share cold-weather stories, including Josh's childhood cowboy boots and a miserable Cleveland Browns vs. Dolphins game. They explain that frostbite is the body's response to protect the core from hypothermia, which is the bigger killer.

segments.title: Blood flow shutdown, hunting response, and ice crystal damage
segments.summary: The hosts describe arteriovenous anastomoses shutting off blood to hands and feet, the hunting response that cyclically reopens them, and its failure near zero degrees Celsius. They explain ice crystals forming between cells, dehydrating them and causing tissue death.

segments.title: Frostnip and the four degrees of frostbite
segments.summary: The hosts distinguish frostnip, which is mild and involves only skin, from frostbite, then go through first-, second-, third- and fourth-degree frostbite, from numbness and blisters to tissue death and likely amputation. They note that repeated freezing and thawing makes damage worse.

segments.title: Rewarming, reperfusion injury, and infection risk
segments.summary: The hosts explain that frostbitten parts should be rewarmed in warm water rather than by direct heat, but only once rescue is assured because refreezing is harmful. They discuss swelling, reperfusion injury, aloe gel, tetanus risk, and walking on frostbitten feet, and the advice to keep moving to maintain circulation.

segments.title: Prevention, myths, body parts at risk, and closing
segments.summary: The hosts cover prevention through layered breathable non-compression clothing, risk from diabetes and thyroid conditions, debunk the idea that body fat protects against cold, and say alcohol and cigarettes are harmful. They discuss why noses run, why ears and cheeks are vulnerable, and close with a hot toddy aside and a listener mail item from Josh Hines about burglar tape.
